passage: Sunday night. Housewarming at Vijay Mama's flat, and I could not wait to leave. He asked, in front of everyone, "So, Preeti, what work are you doing now?" I heard myself say, "Logistics." My aunt nodded, impressed. I said nothing else, my face burning. The truth is I deliver food from seven to midnight, saving for my exam course, and I like the freedom. But in that room it felt like something to hide. Sitting on the bus home, I wondered what I was ashamed of. It is honest work. Next time, I will tell Mama plainly: I deliver food now, I am saving for my course, and I plan to change by next March. Lying makes me feel smaller than the job does.

qa.q: What work did Preeti tell Vijay Mama she was doing?
Why did Preeti's face burn at the housewarming?
qa.a: She felt a private sting of shame because her relatives see delivery work as low status, and she had not told them the truth.

qa.q: What could Preeti say to her relatives next time?
qa.a: She can say plainly that she delivers food, is saving for her exam course, and plans to move on by next March.

qa.q: How might Vijay Mama react when Preeti tells him the truth?
qa.a: He may be surprised, and may or may not approve at first, since relatives see the work as low status. A clear plan and timeline may help him understand she is being serious.

grounding: The protagonist hides that she delivers food because relatives see it as low status, then decides to state it honestly with her plan.

passage: At his cousin Tanuja's engagement in Jalandhar, Baljeet kept his phone face down so no one would see the delivery app's orange screen. When Tayaji asked what he was doing these days, he said, 'Something in logistics,' and steered the talk to cricket. He had been riding for four months since his engineering results came out badly, and every lie made him feel smaller. Then, halfway through dinner, his phone chimed loudly: 'Your pickup is ready.' Tanuja, sitting next to him, glanced at the screen. Later, by the sweets table, she said quietly, 'You deliver food? Why hide it?' 'Because they'll say I've fallen.' 'You're paying for your re-exam yourself. That's not falling.' Before leaving, Baljeet told Tayaji the truth, and his plan: ride until the re-exam in June, then apply for site engineer jobs. Tayaji grunted, then said, 'Good. Honest work.' His face still burned, but less.

qa.q: What did Baljeet first tell Tayaji he was doing?
How did Baljeet feel each time he lied?
qa.a: Baljeet felt smaller and ashamed, afraid relatives would say he had fallen.

qa.q: What made Baljeet's final answer to Tayaji wise?
qa.a: He told the truth and shared a clear plan: riding until the June re-exam, then applying for site engineer jobs.

qa.q: How does Tanuja see Baljeet's job?
qa.a: Tanuja sees it as honest work that pays for his re-exam, not a fall.

grounding: Shows a young man hiding food-delivery work from relatives out of shame, then explaining it honestly with a plan and timeline.

passage: For three months Zainab had told her Khala and cousins in Lucknow that she worked at a call centre. In truth she delivered groceries on her scooter across Gomti Nagar, in a helmet that hid her face when she passed their street. The money paid for her typing course. But the lie had a cost: she had stopped going to the course on Saturdays in case a cousin saw her near the institute. On Friday her friend Anand, who rode for the same company, asked why she had missed class twice. 'In case someone sees me in the uniform,' she said. Anand shrugged. 'Your Khala sells pickles from home. Is that low?' Zainab laughed despite herself. That night at dinner she told Khala everything: the scooter, the money, the typing course, the plan to apply for office jobs by December. Khala was quiet, then said, 'Next time you're in our lane, stop for tea.' On Saturday Zainab went to class.

qa.q: What had Zainab told her Khala she did?
qa.a: Zainab had said she worked at a call centre.

qa.q: What was Zainab afraid of when she skipped the Saturday class?
qa.a: Zainab was afraid and ashamed that a cousin might see her in the delivery uniform.
Telling Khala the truth and the December plan, because it ended the lie and let her return to the course that was the point of the work.

qa.q: How does Anand see Zainab's worry about status?
qa.a: Anand sees nothing low in honest work and gently points out that Zainab's Khala also works from home.

grounding: Shows the private sting of hiding delivery work from relatives, the lie starting to stall her progress, and honesty about the plan setting it right.
